To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an exercise‐associated increase occurs in both hs‐cTNI and NT‐pro‐BNP in both adolescents and adults.

the cardiac biomarkers high‐sensitivity troponin T and N‐terminal probrain‐natriuretic peptide are elevated following a maximal swimming exercise test in adolescents with different levels of pubertal maturation and adults.
the release of cardiac biomarkers after exercise is similar in adolescents and adults and that the male participants had higher levels of hs‐c TnT than female participants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise on cardiac biomarkers in male and female adolescents and adults.
the effects of acute exercise on cardiac troponin and natriuretic peptides in adolescent swimmers with different pubertual status.
the effects of endurance exercise on cardiac troponin and brain natriuretic peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

hs‐cTNT is a biomarker that increases with exercise in both male and female adolescents and adults, but NT‐proBNPT is a biomarker of exercise that is not influenced by sex or pubertal status in adolescents and adults.
hs‐cTnl is a sensitive marker of myocardial damage, but it does not reflect the severity of the damage, and the release of NT‐proBNPs is a sensitive marker for myocardial stretch.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present data support that the use of hs‐cTN and NT‐proBPNP for the diagnosis of myocardial injury is independent of sex and pubertal status, although the use of hs-cTnT in clinical practice is not supported by the present data.
exercise‐associated biomarker release is similar in male and female adolescents and adults.

the present study shows that the cardiac biomarker responses to exercise are similar between adolescents and adults, and that there are sex differences in the cardiac troponin response to exercise, but not in NT‐proB‐NP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of hs‐c‐TnT and/or NT‐proBNPt in the context of endurance exercise should be interpreted with caution, particularly in adolescent and young adult athletes, as there is considerable overlap in the upper limits of the reference ranges.
exercise‐induced release of cardiac biomarkers occurs in both adolescents and adults and is not influenced by pubertal status, although substantial individual variability was observed.
the hs‐cTNT response to a single bout of exercise is not affected by pubertal status in adolescents, but the response is greater in males compared with females.
